entities.title: Why zazzle is not freestanding on macOS
entities.summary: On macOS zazzle links libSystem and is entered at main, because the kernel kills a Mach-O without dyld; only its system calls stay raw.
entities.context: zazzle exists to start as fast as possible, and on Linux it is a static executable with no libc and its own `_start`. The same on macOS would avoid dyld and libSystem.

options.title: A static Mach-O with its own entry
options.consequences: A statically linked Mach-O with a valid ad-hoc signature and LC_UNIXTHREAD is killed (`Killed: 9`) on exec on macOS 26, and the linker refuses dynamic executables that skip libSystem.

options.title: Link libSystem, enter at main, keep raw system calls
options.consequences: The startup floor on macOS is dyld plus libSystem (the README's Measurements give the timings), so zazzle can match but not beat a libSystem hello there.

entities.decision: On macOS the Makefile defines ZAZZLE_LIBSYSTEM and links normally; entry.h then provides `main`, and the syscalls stay raw.
entities.rationale: It is the only kind of executable macOS runs. Where the spawn itself costs too much, `zazzled mcp` avoids it entirely.
